en: And the eardrums of lesser men
Simply burst.
The signal was firmly sounded,
And the many warriors who had hung the cauldron
All mounted their horses.
If battle brings a mighty clash,
What regret could the people have?
Then Kanchoro shouted,
And at the beginning of his speech
Called out as though bearing glad tidings:
“O my dears, have you seen what I have seen?
Külchoro and Semetey,
You two glorious heroes, make ready!
Have you sensed what I have sensed?
A massed host comes without breaking formation,
And within that host
Comes a fire blazing like a beacon,
An army that will burn all in its path;
When an army comes, it comes in multitudes,
Like a deep-dug trench and rampart.
Raising their tasseled banners,
Enemies of every kind are coming.
When I behold the approaching host
And pray for the people’s safety,
I see the vast army of the Jediger,
So vast the earth seems to bend beneath it.
I heard reports from those who came:
They say it encamped along the Jetisuu;
They say Kyyaz, hero of the Jediger,
Has become a thousand times
Greater than brave Toltoy.
Keeping court and reigning as khan,
Growing overbearing and ruling the people,
With houses spread across the hills,
Among the Jediger of Jetisuu
He has become the sole sovereign khan.
The generous Jediger people
Are now a body without a head,
Subdued by brave Kyyaz;
He comes ravaging lands and driving nations before him,
Leading his lions onward.
He comes leading heroes whose blows
Would scatter carrion to the winds,
Leading lions who spill blood
Whenever they enter combat.
A host of countless thousands comes,
Not a small force but a multitude;
If we rush boastfully into battle,
Our fleeting lives will face great peril.
No man could defeat them;
No stratagem could hold out against them.
No envoy could pass between us,
And none who meet them will survive.
Divided into many formations,
The Jediger warriors
Appear almost numberless.
Along the shore road by Kum-Kyya,
They come pouring forth,
Swarming so thickly they seem like worms,
Streaming out in splendor.
Over the ridge at Kötörmö
Their multitude comes pouring forth;
The front ranks of noble
Hero Kyyaz are appearing.
Along the edge of Suusamyr
Half his host is descending;
Along Bek-Jailoo
His khan’s own force comes forth.
From Kara-Buura and Chatkal,
The Jediger, covering the land like sand,
Are also pouring out.
Through every valley, billowing,
Their dust rises;
As they march in a roaring surge,
Their dust rises.
Anyone who sees or hears of them
Feels his soul leave his body.
They have fitted their hollow-shafted spears
With shafts of hard wood,
Saying, ‘Either we shall utterly destroy them,
And slaughter the gray wolf, the blood-drinker,
Semetey,
Or else we ourselves shall die;
We have marched from Jetisuu
To this place from which there is no retreat,
And now that we have come, we shall see it through.’
Their moonlike tasseled banners fly,
Their clamor splits the sky,
Their army rends the earth;
In Jetisuu the Jediger
Have risen to the last man,
Not a few but a multitude,
And Kyyaz drives them onward.
Swarming like worms, the Jediger,
The fierce khan Kyyaz’s host,
Come streaming forth in splendor.
The swordsmen are at the front,
The Jediger seething and hissing,
With their strongest men along the flanks.
The axemen are at the front,
Their shouts loud enough to split heads;
The Jediger advance
With their champions on the flanks.
The musketeers are at the front;
The Jediger swarm like worms,
With their finest men along the flanks,
Firing muskets and loosing arrows,
Advancing in battle array.
Thrusting spears and striking with axes,
The Jediger, bound by their oath,
Come flooding forward.
They come to settle Zhylygnduu, broad Keng-Kol,
And spacious Talas;
Grappling like dragons,
Thrusting spears in glittering ranks,
Piercing lungs and severing heads,
They come to conquer and occupy it.
The Jediger will surely destroy
The small folk who think themselves mighty,
And bring calamity upon them;
They will surely make the girls whimper
And drag them away as plunder.
Saying, ‘We have avenged Toltoy,’
They will surely crush everything to dust.
The valiant men and khans,
Every son who has been born,
And all the countless living souls—
They will surely slaughter them all.
The ninety thousand horses in the mountains
They will surely raid without pause.
The surging Jediger
Will surely reach our very roots;
All the people they have ruined
They will surely drive away as captives.
The girls will whimper without ceasing,
Becoming precious spoils.
The Jediger are seething;
They will surely drink much blood.
Their warriors, surging rank upon rank,
Looked ominous to my eyes.
If the raging Jediger gray wolves
Overflow their bounds and attack,
How could any man withstand them?
The seething Jediger
Are fearsome indeed—
Could even all the peoples of the age endure them?
Shamed at our own hearth,
Are we to die in panic?
Shall we submit to the Jediger,
Lead camels as tribute,
And surrender untold livestock,
Only to die an ignoble death?
Whimpering like young puppies,
Are we to die dishonorably?
Know that Kyyaz comes in might,
Bringing great peril to our precious lives.
The chestnut horse beneath him
Is a steed that flies like a cloud,
And brave Kyyaz upon it
Is worth a thousand men.
Kalcha and Kadyrbai,
And below them Tölöbai,
Have a force of some four thousand men.
In his wrath he seems able
To reduce the whole world to servitude;
If he battles the world,
He seems able to leave slaughter in his wake.
When he stiffens in fury,
He could turn the waters of a river;
Anyone who provokes his vengeance,
The roused Jediger
Could kill and crush to dust.
Sending armies in from all four sides,
Trampling wherever they reach,
Grinding it beneath the earth,
They could spread out their sevenfold host.
Smashing mountains and rocks,
They could march on, leaving a broad black road;
If they close in savage combat,
They could crush anyone they encounter.
Even if all the peoples of the world arose,
Not a few but a multitude,
Damn those Jediger—
They could overrun them in a single campaign.
Anyone who crosses them
Will behold the face of Judgment Day;
If they fight in burning wrath,
Not only the Kyrgyz—
They could divide all the peoples of the age.
Whoever beholds their fury
Would cry, ‘Mercy, my lord, I submit!’
And fall prostrate before them,
Surrendering utterly.
Silver-eyed and sun-faced,
My roaring heroic uncle,
You yourself are here,
And the true hero, ever ready for war,
Your matchless eagle Külchoro,
Your warrior, is here.
Let us halt the Jediger army,
Take fine horses from our pastures,
Load up treasure and gold,
Clothe them in sumptuous robes,
Choose beautiful girls for them,
And mount them on swift horses;
Perhaps we should present all this
To the vast Jediger people.
Let us neither quarrel nor feud,
Nor wage war before a year has passed.
Let us not fight until not one
Solitary soul remains.
Let us accept their demands
And pay all their tribute.
Let us obey what they say,
Turn our stallions’ heads,
Raise our hands amid the tumult,
And declare that we submit.
Let us give camels as tribute,
And give them many people as tribute;
Let us accept their demands
And give them whatever they ask.
Let us neither quarrel nor feud,
But preserve our people.
From this tumultuous conflict
Let us escape safe and sound.
Let us say, ‘Our roots and souls are one;
We have been kin from the beginning,’
And offer them reasoned words.
Let us stand against this flood
And survive safe and sound.
Let us gather the daughters
Of the Argyn and the Kyrgyz
And lead them forth in procession.
Offering girls, let us say, ‘We submit;
Brave Kyyaz, halt!’
Let us give him skilled young women,
Girls in red dresses with moon-slender waists,
Graceful, playful girls,
And ask him to restrain his army.
May our cherished people survive unharmed
And return safely to their villages.
Let us become in-laws, exchanging livestock,
Clasp hands, and share rich butter,
Eat meat from a single platter,
Meet face-to-face as kinsmen,
Declare the blood-price for Toltoy,
And offer apologies and gifts.
Let us make Talas our shared land
And the Jediger our people;
Let us all settle together
And become newfound kin.
Let us accept what he says;
Let us place both reins and the single bridle
In his hands now,
Telling him to put the people in order.
Let us proclaim to the nation
